name: rpcclient
one_line: talk to a Windows or Samba machine over MS-RPC
plain: `rpcclient` connects to a Windows (or Samba) host over SMB and runs remote procedure calls: list users, groups and shares, read the password policy, translate names to SIDs. It is a staple of Windows enumeration in labs.
A null session (empty user and password) is accepted by some old or misconfigured hosts. Modern ones refuse it; with valid credentials you can usually do much more.
when: Read the password policy before any guessing.
Look up a user's full details or their group memberships.

examples.title: Null session
examples.explain: -U '' is an empty user, -N means no password. If it connects you land at an `rpcclient $>` prompt.

examples.title: With credentials
examples.explain: The format is DOMAIN\user%password. Use -U alice and type the password when asked to keep it out of the history.

examples.title: One command, then exit
examples.explain: -c runs a command and returns, good for scripts.

examples.title: List users and groups
examples.explain: Prints names with their RIDs (numeric ids). The rid 0x1f4 is Administrator.

examples.title: Details of one user
examples.explain: queryuser shows a user's full record; querygroupmem lists the members of a group by RID.

examples.title: Password policy
examples.explain: Shows the minimum length and the lockout rules: read it before attempting any password guessing.

examples.title: Domain info
examples.explain: Domain name, SID and server details.

examples.title: Names and SIDs
examples.explain: Translates between account names and SIDs.

examples.title: Shares
examples.explain: Lists the shares the server offers.

mistakes: Expecting a null session to work on a current Windows host: try credentials, or another tool.
Forgetting that RIDs are hex (0x1f4 not 1f4 when typed).
Putting a password in -U in the shell history: set it interactively or use -A.
Ignoring the password policy and locking accounts out in a lab you share.
try: Connect to a lab host with a null session and run srvinfo.
Enumerate users and groups, then query the first three users.
Read the password policy and write down the lockout threshold.
see_also: smbclient(1), enum4linux(1), ldapsearch(1), net(8), nmap(1) (smb-* scripts), impacket, crackmapexec / netexec.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
